s: a third-floor rooftop over Bukchon's sea of hanok tiled roofs
w: A quiet café inside Bukchon Hanok Village whose real draw is up a flight of stairs -- a third-floor rooftop terrace looking straight across the tiled roofs of one of Seoul's last intact traditional neighbourhoods. Calm and unhurried, a ten-minute walk from Anguk Station but a world away from its foot traffic.
_facts: Located at 64 Bukchon-ro, Gahoe-dong, Jongno District, Seoul, about 10 minutes' walk from Anguk Station Exit 2
Known for its third-floor rooftop terrace overlooking Bukchon Hanok Village's tiled roofs
Set inside the historic hanok neighbourhood

s: the world's first sheep café, tucked in a Hongdae basement
w: Billed as the world's first sheep café, this Hongdae basement spot lets customers share a waffle or bingsu with a small flock of live sheep wandering the room. A genuinely odd, kid-in-a-petting-zoo experience folded into an otherwise ordinary café menu, a short walk from Hongik University Station.
_facts: Located in the basement of Seogyo Prugio Shopping Mall, 10 Hongik-ro, Mapo-gu, Seoul, near Hongik University Station Exit 9
Known as the world's first sheep café, with live sheep sharing the café space with customers
Serves waffles, bingsu and kombucha alongside coffee

s: a poop-themed café on the 4th floor of the Ssamziegil complex
w: A cheerfully committed poop-themed café inside Insadong's Ssamziegil shopping complex -- toilet-shaped mugs, poop-shaped pastries, and decor that leans fully into the joke rather than softening it. One of Seoul's more determinedly silly theme cafés, and a genuine local curiosity rather than a one-off gimmick.
_facts: Located on the 4th floor of the Ssamziegil Building, 38 Gwanhun-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul, Insadong
Poop-themed café known as Ddong Café ("ddong" means poop in Korean)
Serves food and drinks styled to match the theme (toilet-shaped mugs, poop-shaped treats)

s: an unfussy, well-regarded roaster holding its own amid Seongsu's pop-up churn
w: A steady, well-regarded café in Seongsu-dong -- the district where Seoul's creative pop-ups and photogenic concept cafés cycle through fastest -- built on consistently good coffee rather than a rotating gimmick. Near Seoul Forest, it draws regulars who want the district's creative energy without the queue for whatever's trending that month.
_facts: Located at 15 Seoulsup 4-gil, Seongdong-gu, Seoul, near Seoul Forest (Seoulsup)
One of several Milestone Coffee locations across Seoul
Known for consistent quality coffee in a district known for fast-turnover trendy cafés

s: an all-white artsy café on the walk to Changdeokgung Palace
w: A minimalist, all-white café on Donhwamun-ro, the street connecting Jongno 3-ga Station to Changdeokgung Palace -- good coffee and food in a gallery-like space that draws a creative crowd without leaning into any single gimmick. A calm stop on the walk to or from one of Seoul's Joseon-era palaces.
_facts: Located at 60 Donhwamun-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul, near Jongno 3-ga Station Exit 7
Known for a minimalist, predominantly white interior design
Sits on the walking route toward Changdeokgung Palace

s: one of Seoul's oldest markets, famous for bindaetteok and mayak kimbap
w: One of Korea's oldest traditional markets, its food alley packed shoulder to shoulder with vendors frying bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and rolling mayak kimbap -- tiny, addictive seaweed rice rolls whose name literally means "drug" kimbap. Textiles and secondhand goods fill the rest of the market, but the food alley is what draws the crowds, day and night.
_facts: Located in Jongno District, Seoul, one of Korea's oldest traditional markets, established 1905
Famous food-alley specialties include bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and mayak ("drug") kimbap
Also sells textiles, hanbok and secondhand goods
